Design language · v2 · measured from two shipping apps

Calm navy surfaces, one blue accent, icons you can read at a glance.

Deckwork is the visual system shared by steamos-fm, a controller-first file manager, and LanWhodis, a network device scanner. It is written down here so a third project can pick it up. Every value on this page was read from the apps' own theme files, and the contrast numbers were measured, not assumed.

Qt Quick / QML3 themes: dark, light, Steam Deck Fluent UI icons, MITOne scale unit: 20 px × zoom

Foundations

Seven rules the rest follows from

These are the decisions that explain most of what you see. When a new screen has to choose, it chooses the way these do.

Layers are steps, not shadows

Each surface sits one clearly visible luminance step above the one beneath it, and edges are 1 px borders. There are no drop shadows. steamos-fm learned this on a handheld: when a button and its panel differed by a single step, the buttons were nearly invisible.

One accent, and it means "you can act on this"

Blue (orange in Steam Deck mode) marks selection, focus and primary actions. Green, amber and red report status. Category colors say what kind of thing a device is. The three never swap jobs.

Shape, color and word, together

A device is a glyph on a tinted tile plus a type label in words. Color alone never carries meaning, so the interface survives color blindness and a washed-out screen.

Pointer and controller first

Rows are 38 px tall at the base scale and text starts at 12 px. Touch works, but it does not set the size. The left stick on a Steam Deck is a precise pointer.

Show the reasoning

Detail panels list the evidence behind a verdict, with weights. Section titles are uppercase and letter-spaced, so a long panel stays scannable.

Every action has a key, and the footer says which

The hint bar is part of the layout. Plain-letter shortcuts are ignored while a text field has focus.

One unit scales everything

Sizes are multiples of a 20 px unit times the user's zoom. Change the unit and the whole interface rescales together.

Foundations

The same language in two apps

Deckwork started in steamos-fm and was refined in LanWhodis. The shared core is the palette, scale, shapes and component vocabulary. Each app adds a few tokens of its own: steamos-fm has file-kind tints and a pane header, LanWhodis has category colors and status tones.

Decisions that came from holding it in your hands

steamos-fm is tested on a handheld (ASUS ROG Ally X, 7 inch panel). Its source records what the device taught the design. These are why several tokens look the way they do.

DateWhat the device showedWhat changed
2026-07-14Buttons and sections were nearly invisible: the secondary fill and the dialog behind it differed by about one luminance step.Added sectionSurface, buttonSurface and their borders, each a deliberate step lighter. Primary buttons moved from a muted accent to the full accent. This is where "layers are steps, not shadows" comes from.
2026-07-18 / 19The controller button legend still read as crowded on real hardware, after the first fix.The gap between legend entries and each glyph-to-label gap were widened twice.
2026-08-01The title bar read as small on the 7 inch panel.A dedicated title-bar scale token, 20% larger, rather than changing the global sizes.

Foundations

Type and scale

The app uses the platform's own interface font (Segoe UI on Windows, DejaVu Sans or the system font on Linux), so it feels native and needs no font files. What is fixed is the scale: five sizes, all multiples of the unit.

Token× unitpx at 1×Used forSample
fontSizeSm0.6212.4Section titles, chips, IP addresses, counts, hint barHue Bridge
fontSize0.7515Body text, buttons, valuesHue Bridge
fontSizeLg0.9519Device names on cards, chrome icon sizeHue Bridge
fontSizeXl1.3527Dialog titles, empty-state headlinesHue Bridge
rowHeight1.938Reference height of a row or control

Weights. Regular for running text and values. Bold for device names, type labels, primary buttons and chips. Nothing in between.

Section titles. Uppercase, bold, fontSizeSm, letter-spacing 0.08 × unit (1.6 px), dim color.

Monospace. IP addresses and MACs only. It makes columns of addresses line up and signals "this is a literal you may copy".

Measure. Detail values wrap at the panel width (about 56 characters at default zoom); long unbroken strings such as service URLs wrap anywhere instead of overflowing.

Foundations

Space and shape

Everything is a multiple of the unit. Corners are generous on large surfaces and tighter on controls. Depth comes from surface color and a hairline border, never from shadow.

Token× unitpx at 1×Used for
unit120The only absolute: 20 px × the user's zoom (70–180%)
pad0.510Inner padding of boxed sections, small gaps
gap0.612Spacing between sibling elements
radius0.510Buttons, inputs, sections, sidebar items, dialogs' fields
radiusLg0.816Device cards, dialogs
Tile radius28% of size–Scales with the tile so a 42 px and a 104 px tile look related
Pillheight ÷ 2–Chips, search field, network picker
Borders–1Always 1 px, except a selected card (2 px accent)
Elevation––None. Use the next surface token: bg → surface → surfaceAlt / dialogSurface

Recipe. A rounded-square tile (radius 28% of its size) filled with the category color at 17% and outlined at 38%. The glyph fills 54% of the tile and uses the full category color.

Chrome icons (search, scan, edit, copy, filters) use the text color, or the accent when active or selected. They sit at about 1.1× the large text size.

Pinning. The bundled set is fetched by a script at a pinned commit, with the MIT notice stored beside it, so it is reproducible and can be refreshed deliberately.

Components

App layout

A fixed shell with three columns. The list is the star; the sidebar filters it and the detail panel explains whatever is selected.

Header3.6u · 72 px · brand, network picker, search, view, export, theme, Scan
Sidebar11.5u · 230 px
icons only: 3.6u
Contentcard grid: columns = ⌊width ÷ 14u⌋, row 6.4u
or list: rows 2.9u
Detail panel21u · 420 px
narrow: 16u
Hint bar1.9u · 38 px · status left, key hints right (hidden when narrow)
Window widthChange
< 1120 pxSidebar collapses to icons only (3.6u).
< 1000 pxDetail panel narrows to 16u, search narrows to 11u, brand tagline and the key-hint legend are hidden.
Minimum900 × 580 px. Below the minimum nothing reflows further, so size down before shipping to a smaller screen.

States of the content area. Before the first scan: a centered tile, a headline, one sentence of reassurance and a single primary button. While the first results arrive: the same hero with a slowly pulsing halo and the live status line. When filters match nothing: a muted icon and a "Clear filters" button.

Feedback. Transient confirmations ("Copied 192.168.1.1", "Saved") appear as a small toast above the hint bar for 2.6 seconds. Long-lived state lives in the hint bar's status line.

Behavior

Motion and states

Motion confirms an interaction and is never decorative. Everything is short, and nothing moves layout.

WhereDurationWhat changes
Buttons, sidebar items, icon buttons90 msFill color (hover, press, selection)
Device cards, search border100–110 msFill and border color
Card press80 msScale to 98.5%
Scan progress line300 ms / 700 msWidth eases to the new value; the bar pulses between 100% and 45% opacity
Empty-state halo900 ms × 2Scale 1.0 → 1.22 → 1.0, sine easing, looping while a scan runs
Toast160 ms + 2.6 sFade in, hold, fade out
StateTreatment
HoverLighter fill; cards also tint their border with the category color at 55%
PressedDarker fill (buttons) or overlay at 16% (icon buttons), cards scale down slightly
SelectedAccent at 20% fill plus a marker (sidebar) or a 2 px accent border on the selected fill (cards)
Focus (keyboard)A 2 px accent ring just outside the control. Inputs also show an accent border.
Disabled40% opacity, no hover
Offline (remembered device)Dimmed tile (glyph at 45%), 55% text, an OFFLINE chip

Behavior

Accessibility audit

Contrast was calculated for the pairs the interface really uses, in all three themes, against WCAG 2.x: 4.5:1 for normal text (including 15 px bold) and 3:1 for icons and large text. The first table is the shared core as LanWhodis ships it. The second is steamos-fm today, which has not adopted these fixes yet.

87 / 87measured pairs meet their target
29 / 29Dark theme
29 / 29Light theme
29 / 29Deck theme

What the core changed, and why

Primary and danger buttons. White text on the bright accent blue was 2.75:1 (Deck orange 2.65:1). Black ink on the bright blue passed, but looked wrong next to light text everywhere else. The core now fills solid buttons with a deeper tone (accentFill, dangerFill) and uses white ink: 5.11:1 on dark, and the hover state stays above 4.5:1. The bright accent stays for icons, focus rings and links.

Dim text. steamos-fm's secondary text color is below 4.5:1 on its dialogs and section boxes. The core's textDim clears 4.5:1 on every panel surface in the dark and Deck themes.

Category colors. Yellow, teal, cyan and orange work as tile glyphs on a dark card but are too light as 15 px label text on white (Smart Home yellow was 1.9:1). The light theme uses darker label variants, drawn through Theme.labelColor; every category label now passes 4.5:1 in every theme.

Status chips. Light-theme chip text uses darker successText, warningText, dangerText tones; dark themes lighten the danger text.

Focus and motion. Keyboard focus is a 2 px accent ring just outside the control. Motion durations go to zero when the operating system asks to reduce motion. Components expose Accessible roles and names.

Scan networkBefore: white on #4a9eff, 2.75:1
Scan networkNow: white on #2a6ccb (accentFill), 5.11:1
Scan networkDeck: white on #b4560a, 4.91:1

Reuse

Tokens as code

The same tokens in two forms. The CSS block is ready for a web project; the QML file is the real theme singleton from the app.

CSS custom properties

/* Deckwork design tokens. Dark is the default; light and Steam Deck override it.
   Solid buttons use --dw-accent-fill / --dw-danger-fill with --dw-accent-ink / --dw-danger-ink. */
:root {
  --dw-unit: 20px;            /* multiply by the user's zoom */
  --dw-font-size-sm: calc(var(--dw-unit) * 0.62);
  --dw-font-size: calc(var(--dw-unit) * 0.75);
  --dw-font-size-lg: calc(var(--dw-unit) * 0.95);
  --dw-font-size-xl: calc(var(--dw-unit) * 1.35);
  --dw-row-height: calc(var(--dw-unit) * 1.9);
  --dw-radius: calc(var(--dw-unit) * 0.5);
  --dw-radius-lg: calc(var(--dw-unit) * 0.8);
  --dw-pad: calc(var(--dw-unit) * 0.5);
  --dw-gap: calc(var(--dw-unit) * 0.6);
  --dw-font: "Segoe UI", system-ui, "DejaVu Sans", sans-serif;

Set data-theme="light" or data-theme="deck" on the root element, or leave it unset for dark. Units: --dw-unit: 20px; derive sizes with calc(var(--dw-unit) * 0.75) so a single zoom variable rescales the page.

Qt Quick: the full Theme.qml singleton

Register it with singleton Theme 1.0 Theme.qml in a qmldir, then bind Theme.mode to your settings.

pragma Singleton
import QtQuick

// Design tokens. Palette and component language follow steamos-fm's Theme.qml (dark navy + blue accent,
// a light mode, and a Steam Deck mode with the orange accent) so the two apps read as a family.
QtObject {
    id: root

    // "dark" | "light" | "deck"   (bound to backend.theme from Main.qml)
    property string mode: "dark"
    property real zoom: 1.0
    // true when the OS asks for reduced motion (bound to backend.reduceMotion from Main.qml)
    property bool reduceMotion: false

    // ── Scale ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    readonly property real unit:       20 * zoom
    readonly property real fontSizeSm: unit * 0.62
    readonly property real fontSize:   unit * 0.75
    readonly property real fontSizeLg: unit * 0.95
    readonly property real fontSizeXl: unit * 1.35
    readonly property real rowHeight:  unit * 1.9
    readonly property real radius:     unit * 0.5
    readonly property real radiusLg:   unit * 0.8
    readonly property real pad:        unit * 0.5
    readonly property real gap:        unit * 0.6
    readonly property bool dark:       mode !== "light"

    // ── Active palette (re-bound on mode change) ──────────────────
    readonly property color bg:             _pal.bg
    readonly property color surface:        _pal.surface
    readonly property color surfaceAlt:     _pal.surfaceAlt
    readonly property color accent:         _pal.accent
    readonly property color accentDim:      _pal.accentDim
    readonly property color selected:       _pal.selected
    readonly property color text:           _pal.text
    readonly property color textDim:        _pal.textDim
    readonly property color divider:        _pal.divider
    readonly property color dialogSurface:  _pal.dialogSurface
    readonly property color dialogBorder:   _pal.dialogBorder
    readonly property color scrim:          _pal.scrim
    readonly property color sectionSurface: _pal.sectionSurface
    readonly property color sectionBorder:  _pal.sectionBorder
    readonly property color buttonSurface:  _pal.buttonSurface
    readonly property color buttonBorder:   _pal.buttonBorder
    readonly property color inputSurface:   _pal.inputSurface
    readonly property color success:        _pal.success
    readonly property color warning:        _pal.warning
    readonly property color danger:         _pal.danger
    // solid button fills are deeper than the accent so white ink clears 4.5:1; the bright accent stays for icons, rings, links
    readonly property color accentFill:      _pal.accentFill   // solid primary-button fill (white ink on it)
    readonly property color dangerFill:      _pal.dangerFill
    readonly property color accentInk:       _pal.accentInk
    readonly property color dangerInk:       _pal.dangerInk
    // status colours tuned for 12 px chip text on their own 16% tint (>= 4.5:1)
    readonly property color successText:    _pal.successText
    readonly property color warningText:    _pal.warningText
    readonly property color dangerText:     _pal.dangerText

    // animation duration in ms; 0 when the user prefers reduced motion
    function dur(ms) { return reduceMotion ? 0 : ms }
    // category label text: the tile colour is fine for icons, but 15 px text needs a per-theme variant (>= 4.5:1)
    function labelColor(darkHex, lightHex) { return mode === "light" ? lightHex : darkHex }
    // accepts a color or a "#rrggbb" string (the model delivers category colours as strings)
    function alpha(c, a) { var q = Qt.color(c); return Qt.rgba(q.r, q.g, q.b, a) }

    property var _pal: _dark
    onModeChanged: {
        switch (mode) {
        case "light": _pal = _light; break
        case "deck":  _pal = _deck;  break
        default:      _pal = _dark;  break
        }
    }

    property var _dark: QtObject {
        readonly property color bg:             "#0e141b"
        readonly property color surface:        "#1a2332"
        readonly property color surfaceAlt:     "#222d3e"
        readonly property color accent:         "#4a9eff"
        readonly property color accentDim:      "#2c5f99"
        readonly property color selected:       "#1e3a5f"
        readonly property color text:           "#e8edf2"
        readonly property color textDim:        "#95a1ae"
        readonly property color divider:        "#2a3545"
        readonly property color dialogSurface:  "#232e3d"
        readonly property color dialogBorder:   "#3c4d61"
        readonly property color scrim:          "#a6040a0d"
        readonly property color sectionSurface: "#1f2a3a"
        readonly property color sectionBorder:  "#33445b"
        readonly property color buttonSurface:  "#33455e"
        readonly property color buttonBorder:   "#5578a3"
        readonly property color inputSurface:   "#0f1722"
        readonly property color success:        "#4cc38a"
        readonly property color warning:        "#e0a84f"
        readonly property color danger:         "#e5534b"
        readonly property color accentFill:      "#2a6ccb"
        readonly property color dangerFill:      "#c93a33"
        readonly property color accentInk:       "#ffffff"
        readonly property color dangerInk:       "#ffffff"
        readonly property color successText:    "#4cc38a"
        readonly property color warningText:    "#e0a84f"
        readonly property color dangerText:     "#ea756f"
    }

    property var _light: QtObject {
        readonly property color bg:             "#f0f4f8"
        readonly property color surface:        "#ffffff"
        readonly property color surfaceAlt:     "#e4e9f0"
        readonly property color accent:         "#1a6bc2"
        readonly property color accentDim:      "#1255a0"
        readonly property color selected:       "#c8dff7"
        readonly property color text:           "#1c2535"
        readonly property color textDim:        "#5d6d80"
        readonly property color divider:        "#d0d8e0"
        readonly property color dialogSurface:  "#ffffff"
        readonly property color dialogBorder:   "#c3cedb"
        readonly property color scrim:          "#66141e2d"
        readonly property color sectionSurface: "#f4f7fb"
        readonly property color sectionBorder:  "#c3cedb"
        readonly property color buttonSurface:  "#e2e9f1"
        readonly property color buttonBorder:   "#93a7bd"
        readonly property color inputSurface:   "#ffffff"
        readonly property color success:        "#2e8f5e"
        readonly property color warning:        "#b87a1c"
        readonly property color danger:         "#c93a33"
        readonly property color accentFill:      "#1a6bc2"
        readonly property color dangerFill:      "#c93a33"
        readonly property color accentInk:       "#ffffff"
        readonly property color dangerInk:       "#ffffff"
        readonly property color successText:    "#26754d"
        readonly property color warningText:    "#8e5e16"
        readonly property color dangerText:     "#b7352e"
    }

    // Steam Deck gaming mode: same navy, orange accent
    property var _deck: QtObject {
        readonly property color bg:             "#0e141b"
        readonly property color surface:        "#1a2332"
        readonly property color surfaceAlt:     "#222d3e"
        readonly property color accent:         "#f38020"
        readonly property color accentDim:      "#c06010"
        readonly property color selected:       "#3d2a18"
        readonly property color text:           "#e8edf2"

        readonly property color dialogSurface:  "#232e3d"
        readonly property color dialogBorder:   "#3c4d61"

Reuse

Prompt for an AI coding assistant

Paste this at the start of a conversation in your friend's project. It carries the tokens, recipes and rules, so the assistant can build in this language without seeing anything else. It names the contrast problem and the fix, so the copy is better than the original.

You are helping me build UI in the "Deckwork" design language, the shared language of steamos-fm and LanWhodis. Follow it closely and ask before you deviate.

CHARACTER
Deep navy surfaces, ONE blue accent, rounded cards, icon tiles tinted by category, boxed sections with small uppercase letter-spaced titles. Calm, dense, friendly to a mouse and a game controller. No drop shadows. No gradients. No emoji as icons.

TOKENS (use the names in code; never hard-code hex inside a component)
Colors are #RRGGBB, except scrim which is #AARRGGBB.
bg: dark #0e141b | light #f0f4f8 | deck #0e141b
surface: dark #1a2332 | light #ffffff | deck #1a2332
surfaceAlt: dark #222d3e | light #e4e9f0 | deck #222d3e
accent: dark #4a9eff | light #1a6bc2 | deck #f38020
accentDim: dark #2c5f99 | light #1255a0 | deck #c06010
selected: dark #1e3a5f | light #c8dff7 | deck #3d2a18
text: dark #e8edf2 | light #1c2535 | deck #e8edf2
textDim: dark #95a1ae | light #5d6d80 | deck #95a1ae
divider: dark #2a3545 | light #d0d8e0 | deck #2a3545
dialogSurface: dark #232e3d | light #ffffff | deck #232e3d
dialogBorder: dark #3c4d61 | light #c3cedb | deck #3c4d61
scrim: dark #a6040a0d | light #66141e2d | deck #a6040a0d
sectionSurface: dark #1f2a3a | light #f4f7fb | deck #1f2a3a
sectionBorder: dark #33445b | light #c3cedb | deck #33445b
buttonSurface: dark #33455e | light #e2e9f1 | deck #34455c
buttonBorder: dark #5578a3 | light #93a7bd | deck #5a7699
inputSurface: dark #0f1722 | light #ffffff | deck #0f1722
accentFill: dark #2a6ccb | light #1a6bc2 | deck #b4560a
dangerFill: dark #c93a33 | light #c93a33 | deck #c93a33
accentInk: dark #ffffff | light #ffffff | deck #ffffff
dangerInk: dark #ffffff | light #ffffff | deck #ffffff
success: dark #4cc38a | light #2e8f5e | deck #4cc38a
warning: dark #e0a84f | light #b87a1c | deck #e0a84f
danger: dark #e5534b | light #c93a33 | deck #e5534b
successText: dark #4cc38a | light #26754d | deck #4cc38a
warningText: dark #e0a84f | light #8e5e16 | deck #e0a84f
dangerText: dark #ea756f | light #b7352e | deck #ea756f
Solid buttons use accentFill / dangerFill with accentInk / dangerInk (white) labels; the bright accent is for icons, focus rings, links and selection.
Category colors (device kinds, never state): Computers #4C8DFF, Mobile #B36BFF, Media #FF7A59, Gaming #2EC4A0, Smart Home #F2B01E, Peripherals #6E8BA8, Network #3FB6E8, Other #8A94A3.

SCALE (everything is a multiple of one unit; unit = 20px x user zoom)
fontSizeSm = 0.62u (12.4px); fontSize = 0.75u (15px); fontSizeLg = 0.95u (19px); fontSizeXl = 1.35u (27px); rowHeight = 1.9u (38px); radius = 0.5u (10px); radiusLg = 0.8u (16px); pad = 0.5u (10px); gap = 0.6u (12px).
Fonts: the platform UI font (Segoe UI / system-ui / DejaVu Sans). Monospace only for IPs, MACs and literals. Weights: regular and bold only.
Section titles: uppercase, bold, fontSizeSm, letter-spacing 0.08u, textDim.

SHAPE AND DEPTH
Radius: 0.5u controls and sections, 0.8u cards and dialogs, pills fully rounded, icon tiles 28% of their size. Borders are always 1px (selected card: 2px accent). Depth comes only from stepping surface colors (bg -> surface -> surfaceAlt / dialogSurface) plus a hairline border. Every layer must be a clearly visible step lighter than the one below it.

RECIPES
- Icon tile: rounded square, fill = category color at 17%, border = 38%, glyph at 54% of the tile in the full category color. Offline: 8% / 15%, glyph at 45% opacity.
- Chip: height 1.3u, pill, fontSizeSm bold, text = tone, fill 16%, border 35%. Tones: neutral(textDim), accent, success, warning, danger.
- Button: height 2.1u, radius 0.5u, 1px border, optional 1.1 x fontSizeLg icon. Default = buttonSurface + buttonBorder. Primary = accentFill with accentInk label, bold. Danger = dangerFill with dangerInk label, bold. Ghost = transparent, no border. Hover lighter (x1.14; only x1.04 on primary and danger so white ink stays above 4.5:1), press darker (x1.18), disabled 40% opacity, keyboard focus is a 2px accent ring just outside the control.
- Device card: radius 0.8u, surface fill, 1px divider; tile left, then name (fontSizeLg bold), type (fontSize bold, category color), IP (fontSizeSm mono, textDim); footer: vendor + status chip. Hover: surfaceAlt fill, border = category color at 55%. Selected: selected fill + 2px accent border.
- Sidebar item: height 2.0u, selected = accent at 20% fill + 4px accent marker + bold; counts in textDim.
- Boxed section: sectionSurface, 1px sectionBorder, radius 0.5u, uppercase title, key/value rows (key 34% textDim, value text).
- Inputs: height 2.1u, inputSurface fill, sectionBorder border, accent border on focus; search is a pill with a leading icon.
- Dialog: dialogSurface, 1px dialogBorder, radius 0.8u, scrim behind it, Escape or scrim click closes, primary action on the right.
- Hint bar: 1.9u footer; status text left, key caps right (1.2u high, 5px radius, text at 8% fill and 22% border).
- Empty state: centered 5.2u tile with a soft pulsing halo, headline fontSizeXl bold, one sentence in textDim, one primary button.
Icons: Fluent UI System Icons (MIT), filled variant, recolored at draw time with the theme color.

BEHAVIOR
Color transitions 90-110ms; card press scales to 98.5% over 80ms; toast fades 160ms and holds 2.6s. Motion never changes layout. Keyboard: arrows move through lists, plain-letter shortcuts are ignored while a text field has focus, and a hint bar teaches the keys. Layout collapses in two steps: the sidebar becomes icons-only below 1120px, then the detail panel narrows and the hint legend hides below 1000px.

ACCESSIBILITY (already built into the tokens above; keep it that way)
- Every text/background pair you introduce must reach 4.5:1 (normal text, including 15px bold); icons and large text 3:1. Measure; do not eyeball.
- Never put white or black text on the bright accent. Use accentFill + accentInk. Hover and press states must keep the ratio.
- Category colors are for glyphs. For label text in the light theme use the darker label variant of each category color.
- Status chip text uses successText / warningText / dangerText, not the raw status colors.
- Focus: a 2px accent ring just outside every focusable element. Honor the OS reduce-motion setting (durations go to 0). Give interactive components accessible roles and names.

HOW TO WORK
1. Ask which stack I use (web, Qt Quick, Flutter, SwiftUI, ...). Do not assume.
2. Create the theme/token file first: all tokens above, three themes, the unit and scale, and a way to switch themes at runtime.
3. Build the primitives next (Button, IconButton, Chip, IconTile, BoxedSection, Input, Dialog, HintBar), each reading only tokens.
4. Then compose screens. Show me screenshots in dark, light and deck before calling anything done.
5. Do not add shadows, gradients, extra accent colors, or color-only status. Status always has a word or an icon too.
6. If something is not covered here, extend the system with the same rules (steps not shadows, one accent, unit multiples) and tell me what you added.

Reuse

Lineage and credits

This language started in steamos-fm. LanWhodis kept its palette and component vocabulary and refined a few tokens on purpose. The core takes the refined values; steamos-fm has not adopted them yet.

Tokensteamos-fm todayDeckwork coreWhy
scrim (dark)Slightly stronger dim behind dialogs
sectionBorder (dark)Softer edge to match the darker section
sectionSurface (dark)Darker, so a section sits between the card and the input
textDim (dark)Lighter, for contrast on cards at 12 px
scrim (light)Slightly stronger dim behind dialogs
sectionBorder (light)Softer edge to match the darker section
sectionSurface (light)Darker, so a section sits between the card and the input
textDim (light)Lighter, for contrast on cards at 12 px
scrim (deck)Slightly stronger dim behind dialogs
sectionBorder (deck)Softer edge to match the darker section
sectionSurface (deck)Darker, so a section sits between the card and the input
selected (deck)
textDim (deck)Lighter, for contrast on cards at 12 px

Added to the core: inputSurface (a darker field for text inputs), success, warning, danger and their text tones, and the solid button tokens accentFill, dangerFill, accentInk, dangerInk.

Stays app-specific in steamos-fm: file-kind tints (archColor, exeColor, mediaColor), rowLine, focusRow, paneHeader and hidColor, which belong to a file browser.

Scale. steamos-fm sizes everything from the shorter screen dimension ÷ 40, because it runs full screen on a handheld. LanWhodis runs in a window, so its unit is a fixed 20 px times the user's zoom.

Icons: Fluent UI System Icons, © Microsoft Corporation, MIT License. Banner fingerprints: Rapid7 Recog, BSD-2-Clause (not part of the visual system).

Source of truth: each app's Theme.qml (LanWhodis: gui/qml/LanWhodis/Theme.qml; steamos-fm: ui/SteamosFM/Theme.qml) and the components beside it. Both repositories are private; everything needed to reuse the language is on this page.
